page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-16 is an Arm-based general purpose virtual machine built on Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors. The configuration provisions 16 dedicated physical cores running at a static 3.0 GHz clock speed, with one execution thread per core. Memory allocation stands at 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a typical 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB per core. The processor implements 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. The instance does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state disks, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and includes zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded execution and solid memory subsystems. In multi-core stress testing and parallel decompression, the instance scores within the middle distribution. It achieves 18.26 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and handles 21.18 million Redis SET operations per second. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 129.41 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measures 67.03 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics reveal notable bottlenecks. Geekbench single-core, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and CPU encryption tests fall into the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural limitations of first-generation Neoverse-N1 execution units relative to modern high-frequency x86 cores.

The qualitative cost profile of the t2a-standard-16 benefits workloads that scale horizontally across physical execution units rather than relying on high per-thread burst speeds. The absence of simultaneous multithreading eliminates noisy neighbor friction across threads within the same physical core. Consequently, the instance functions effectively for containerized microservices, Clang-based software compilation pipelines, web application tiers, and intermediate caching layers, while remaining suboptimal for heavy single-thread processing or large language model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-16 is a general purpose virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit Arm architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical vCPUs powered by Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processors operating at 3.0 GHz, paired with 64 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Because each vCPU corresponds to a full physical core without simultaneous multithreading, the instance delivers consistent execution characteristics across parallel operations. Benchmark testing demonstrates solid average throughput in multi-core CPU evaluation, static web serving at 18.26 GB/sec, and Redis in-memory operations reaching 21.18 million operations per second. However, single-threaded execution and specialized cryptographic tests register below average compared to contemporary x86 alternatives. The instance does not include bundled local storage or discrete graphics processing units, requiring external persistent disks for stateful data. It delivers favorable resource efficiency for horizontally scaled environments, containerized microservices, software compilation with Clang, and web serving.
